title: TE Robert L. Reymond et al. v. Illiana Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained in all parts: Item 1 (failure to take appropriate BCO 34-7 action concerning a teaching elder) sustained; Item 2 (improper reduction of charges from original findings and the final Presbytery action) sustained. The case was sent back to Illiana Presbytery for a new trial. The recommendation was adopted, directing Presbytery to follow BCO disciplinary procedures because the record showed inconsistencies in applying BCO Part II.
first_summary: A complaint challenged Illiana Presbytery's handling of a teaching elder: after he confessed adultery, Presbytery charged him only with ninth-commandment violations, admonished him, and required him to reconsider his call. The complaint alleged failure to follow BCO 34-7 and improper reduction of charges. The Commission sustained both complaint items and sent the case back for a new trial. It reasoned that confessed sins were not considered and the censure was not commensurate with the offenses charged, and directed BCO compliance.
summary: A teaching elder confessed adultery, but Presbytery charged him only with ninth-commandment violations, admonished him, and required him to reconsider his call. The complaint alleged Presbytery failed to take BCO 34-7 action and improperly reduced the charges. The Commission sustained both items and remanded for a new trial, reasoning that the confessed sins were not considered and the censure was not commensurate with the offenses charged; it did not itself convict or sentence him. It adopted a recommendation directing Presbytery to follow BCO disciplinary procedures.
